blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Accuracy, consistency and transparency sound simple in a training room. In practice, they are decisions made dozens of times a week. Should this expense go under 'marketing' or 'sales'? Does that legal fee belong to this project or the next one? Should we capitalise this purchase or treat it as an expense?

Each choice, alone, looks small. Together, they shape whether the numbers mean the same thing month after month. A good accountant writes down the rule the first time a grey area appears, and then follows it — even when following it is slightly inconvenient.

Principles that live in a document are worthless. Principles that live in daily decisions, quietly, are what make the books trustworthy.

items.q: According to the text, when do accuracy, consistency and transparency actually get tested?
options: When a new accountant is hired
In dozens of small decisions made every week
items.why: "In practice, they are decisions made dozens of times a week."

items.q: What should a good accountant do the first time a grey area appears?
options: Write down the rule and then follow it
Wait until the pattern becomes clearer
Choose whichever option looks best that month
items.why: "A good accountant writes down the rule the first time a grey area appears, and then follows it."

items.q: What makes the numbers "mean the same thing month after month"?
options: The many small choices being made consistently
Keeping the principles in a document
Treating each choice as small and independent
items.why: "Together, they shape whether the numbers mean the same thing month after month."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A written policy is enough to guarantee good books.
Consistency matters as much as getting a single figure right.
Small classification choices add up to something meaningful.
Following a rule is worth it even when it is inconvenient.
items.why: Inferência: "Principles that live in a document are worthless" — o documento sozinho não basta.

items.q: The phrase "even when following it is slightly inconvenient" suggests that…
options: rules should be broken when they are hard to apply
doing the right thing sometimes costs a little effort or comfort
items.why: Inferência: o valor está em manter a regra mesmo quando dá um pouco de trabalho seguir.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte gravando um memorando interno para a equipe. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Morning, everyone. I'm recording this instead of writing three separate emails, because the point applies to all of us.

Last week I reviewed the ledger and found the same kind of expense — a supplier onboarding fee — booked three different ways by three of you. One person put it under marketing, one under sales, and one capitalised it. None of you was careless. Each choice was defensible on its own. That's exactly the problem: when a grey area has no rule, three sensible people will reach three sensible answers, and the books stop meaning one thing.

So here is what I'd like. From today, the first time any of you hits a case that isn't obvious, don't just decide quietly — write the rule down in the shared classification note and flag it to me. We'll agree it once, and then we all follow it, every month, even when the tidy answer would look a little better on the report.

I know this feels slower. It isn't. Redoing a quarter's entries because nobody wrote the rule down — that is what's slow. Consistency is the boring part, and it's the part clients actually trust us for.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why is Charlotte recording a memo instead of writing separate emails?
options: The same point applies to everyone on the team
She wanted a permanent audio record for the auditor
items.why: "because the point applies to all of us."

items.q: What did Charlotte find when she reviewed the ledger?
options: The same expense booked three different ways
A missing capitalisation on a large purchase
Three duplicate payments to one supplier
items.why: "the same kind of expense… booked three different ways by three of you."

items.q: What does Charlotte want the team to do the first time they hit an unclear case?
options: Book it under marketing by default
Ask the client how to classify it
Write the rule in the shared note and flag it to her
items.why: "write the rule down in the shared classification note and flag it to me."

items.q: When Charlotte says "None of you was careless," she is suggesting that…
options: the problem is the missing rule, not the people
the team needs more training in accounting
the errors were too small to matter
items.why: Inferência: cada escolha era razoável; o que falta é uma regra combinada, não competência.

items.q: What does Charlotte imply about the 'slower' feeling of writing rules down?
options: It genuinely slows the team down, but is worth it
It will speed up client approvals
It matters less than getting each number exactly right
It only feels slow — redoing a quarter's entries is the real delay
items.why: Inferência: "I know this feels slower. It isn't. Redoing a quarter's entries… that is what's slow."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We treated the software licence as an ordinary expense rather than an asset." An expense is…
options: a cost recorded against the period's profit
a long-term asset on the balance sheet
items.why: Expense = despesa: um custo lançado contra o resultado do período.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "When it isn't clear where a cost belongs, you are in a ___ and need a written rule."
items.why: Grey area = área cinzenta: o caso que não é obviamente de um lado ou de outro.

items.q: "We decided to capitalise the new server rather than expense it." To capitalise means to…
options: delete the cost from the accounts
charge it entirely to this month
pass the cost to the client
record the cost as an asset and spread it over time
items.why: To capitalise = capitalizar: registrar como ativo e reconhecer o custo ao longo do tempo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A policy that nobody applies in daily work is essentially ___."
items.why: Worthless = sem valor: princípios que ficam só no papel não valem nada.

items.q: "Transparency, here, means…"
options: recording what actually happened, not what looks best
sharing every figure with the public
items.why: Transparency = transparência: registrar o que de fato aconteceu, não o que fica mais bonito.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em reuniões de finanças e contabilidade. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The controller still has to sign off on the new classification rule." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the shared classification note across all three teams next week." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, colocar em prática.

items.q: "Two accountants pushed back on the new rule at first." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Everyone agreed the policy, but nobody followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it out to the end
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Fixing one mislabelled invoice won't move the needle on how consistent the books are." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
